transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Zephyr), Marcus Lee (Zephyr), Derek Nguyen (Zephyr)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy):
- Kickoff/handoff from sales to success/ops; focus on runtime sizing, VPC/private deployment questions, security artifacts and timeline for pilot.
- Primary success criteria: <5 00 ms p95 for user-facing features, cost target <$0.01 per 1k tokens (ballpark), audit logs enabled.
- Actionable next steps: runbook, sizing spreadsheet, VPC peering details, schedule network walkthrough.

Topics: onboarding runbook, Dedicated vs Hosted, VPC peering, KMS/HSM for keys, SOC2/compliance docs, test dataset and evals, rollout plan (canary), staging access and credentials, monitoring & alerting (Redwood Console).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna just do like a quick activation handoff and runtime intake, i've got priya here from the eng team, uh she's the se who's gonna drive the sizing and runtime notes.
[00:17] Priya (Redwood SE): hey all, hi lina, marcus, derek, thanks for carving out time. quick ask: if you can have your traffic profile ready — qps, typical sequence lengths — that'll help.
[00:30] Lina (Zephyr): yeah yeah, thanks. we tried to put that into the intake form but it's pretty rough, we have a couple of product flows, primary is customer support summarization which is low qps but strict latency, and a batch embed job for search that can tolerate higher latency.
[00:45] Marcus (Zephyr): to add, timeline is kinda urgent for us, pilot needs to be ready in three weeks, that's internal timeline from the product team.
[00:55] Jordan: noted. three weeks is tight but doable for a pilot — depends on network work and whether you go hosted or dedicated. can we talk about their tradeoffs now?
[01:10] Derek (Zephyr): sure, we were leaning to Redwood Dedicated because of predictable throughput and data separation, but curious about cost delta vs hosted. Also need to confirm we can use our KMS and existing SSO.
[01:25] Priya: Dedicated will give you reserved GPU pools — predictable p99s — but there's a ramp and we need infra details for peering. Hosted is faster to get started but you'd be on shared infra; data controls are stronger with dedicated or Private/VPC. small note, sometimes the transcript has product names off — we run as "Redwood Dedica" in older notes lol.
[01:45] Marcus: haha that's fine. security is non-negotiable for us — SOC 2 and audit logs; we need to know retention windows and whether logs can stream to our SIEM.
[02:02] Jordan: yes, we support exporting audit logs and can map retention windows, i'll attach the SOC2 and security pack after. priya, can you summarize where we'd need derek's team to jump in?
[02:15] Priya: sure — top three items: 1) VPC peering or private link details (CIDR, firewall rules), 2) IAM contacts + SAML metadata for SSO, 3) any egress rules for third-party analytics. plus a small list of test credentials.
[02:34] Derek: we can get the CIDRs and an outboard infrastructure engineer to share that by friday, 2026-07-23.
[02:42] Jordan: perfect. ok let's pivot to runtime sizing — priya?
[02:49] Priya: based on what you told us: two primary workloads. For the support summarization: p95 latency goal <500ms, qps ~2-5 at peak. For the embedding batch job: qps bursts of up to 50 but can be batched overnight. We'll propose a baseline of 2 small GPU nodes with autoscale for bursts, or a single dedicated medium pool depending on your concurrency. note: quantization options can reduce memory but may trade off some quality on older open models.
[03:26] Marcus: how do we evaluate that tradeoff? our quality bar is quite high for summarization.
[03:34] Priya: we run prompt evals and can do a regression harness — you give us a seed set of 50 examples, we'll run A/B against quantized and full-fp models and report rouge/metric diffs. also our Optimize tool can recommend quant profiles.
[03:50] Lina: ok we can prepare that. also how does caching work? we have recurring prefixes in support chats.
[03:58] Priya: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching — it'll help reduce token cost for repeated context. for your low-latency flows we might enable a small in-memory KV cache on the node. caching also influences routing decisions. sometimes notes will say "KV cash" in the raw transcript due to speech-to-text.
[04:18] Derek: network constraints — our infra team might require that the initial pilot stays in our VPC and we use private deployment. is that possible on a pilot timeline?
[04:29] Jordan: yes, Private/VPC is an option but it's more work upfront; Dedicated with VPC peering could be a middle ground. we'll need your network team to sign a short peering checklist.
[04:40] Marcus: about credentials — can we use our HSM for key management? we are using an on-prem HSM for secrets.
[04:48] Priya: we integrate with customer-managed KMS, and for some Private installs we support HSM/HSM-backed key wraps. we'll follow up with detail in the security doc.
[04:58] Lina: awesome. also, who will be our primary CSM contact? we want a single thread for issues during pilot.
[05:05] Jordan: i'll be your owner for commercial and success until handoff, and priya will be technical lead for the onboarding. you'll also get a dedicated CSM for the go-live stage — i'll introduce them in the next email.
[05:17] Marcus: great. ok let's surface potential blockers from our side — networking and legal. legal needs an NDA addendum for data processing because some support transcripts contain pii.
[05:30] Jordan: understood; we have a standard DPA and can do addendum. i'll route that to your legal.

[05:40] (15 minute marker)
[05:40] Priya: quick callout on metrics: we'll instrument latency traces to Redwood Console and provide token-level cost estimates; but to get precise per-route cost we need sample traffic and prompt lengths.
[05:55] Marcus: we can give you a week of logs from the current system but anonymized; would that suffice?
[06:02] Priya: yes anonymized logs are great; we'll use them to calibrate batch sizes and buffer configs.
[06:09] Derek: on the staging setup — what credentials do you need from our side and how do you prefer them transmitted?
[06:16] Jordan: we'll use our secure credential exchange (we have a vault link), but for VPC peering you'll just share a ticket with a contact and we'll coordinate a maintenance window.

[06:30] Lina: on the pilot success criteria — product asked for p95 < 500ms for support, and embeddings accuracy drop no more than 2% vs baseline. also cost target was mentioned but it's flexible.
[06:44] Priya: we'll turn those into measurable SLOs in the runbook and add regression alerts in Redwood Optimize.

[07:00] Marcus: curious about fallback strategies — if Dedicated nodes become overloaded do you fail to hosted? we need graceful degradation.
[07:10] Priya: yes we can configure smart routing and fallbacks: canary to a cheaper hosted variant when Dedicated is at capacity, or queue/scale policies. fallback latency will be higher but keeps requests flowing. we'll document fallback policies and expected p95s for each tier. "smart routing" sometimes appears in our notes as "smart routin'" from speech.
[07:28] Derek: what's the expected lead time for Dedicated pool provisioning?
[07:33] Jordan: typically 3-7 business days once contract and capacity are confirmed; quicker in many cases if we have availability in region. for private/on-prem it'll be longer.
[07:44] Marcus: and pricing — can you give a ballpark for the Dedicated option vs hosted?
[07:50] Jordan: i'll send a tailored quote; high-level, Dedicated has a monthly base for reserved capacity plus token costs; hosted is pure usage. we'll avoid numbers on the call but i'll follow up in the email with ranges.

[08:05] (10 minute deep-dive)
[08:05] Priya: technical nit: for your summarization pipeline we recommend using a medium sequence length profile to optimize kernel selection. That influences our kernel selection and batching. if you often go to 2k tokens we'll pick different execution kernels.
[08:24] Marcus: our longest flow is about 1.2k tokens typically, but there are edge cases.
[08:30] Priya: that's good — 1.2k is manageable; we'll size memory accordingly. we'll also run a KV cache sensitivity test because long sequences + KV cache can change memory footprint.
[08:44] Lina: any troubleshooting playbook we should expect? we don't want to be blocked when calls time out.
[08:51] Priya: we'll provide runbook sections: initial health checks, how to read traces in Redwood Console, common errors (OOMs, network timeouts), and escalation path. expected triage time during pilot is same day for Sev1 in business hours.

[09:10] Derek: re: observability — can logs be forwarded to our Splunk?
[09:15] Jordan: yes, audit logs and usage logs can be exported; metrics can be forwarded via prometheus endpoints or to cloud metrics, and we can stream logs to your SIEM.
[09:24] Marcus: ok that's important.

[10:00] (short silence, background noise)
[10:20] Priya: small gotcha: when we do quantization recommendations, sometimes there is a small regression in some edge prompts; we use the eval harness to detect those before rollouts.
[10:36] Lina: good — we'll prepare a set of edge-case prompts.

[12:05] (mid-call clarifications)
[12:05] Marcus: what's the process for canary rollouts? we want A/B tests with 10% traffic to start.
[12:13] Priya: we support canary rollouts and A/B routing via the Console. you can set percentage rollouts and automatic rollback on quality regressions. we'll help set up the first rollout.
[12:26] Jordan: and priya will coordinate the canary spec with your SRE.

[15:00] (customer questions ramp up)
[15:00] Derek: who is the contact for compliance questions?
[15:06] Jordan: our security lead is Mara Kline — i'll copy her in the security bundle email; she handles SOC2, ISO, and data residency.
[15:15] Marcus: speaking of data residency — our EU customers need data stored in eu-west. is regional pinning possible?
[15:22] Priya: yes — we can pin deployments to regions; we'll discuss region availability when we send the runbook. sometimes transcripts list region as just "E U west" — small tts weirdness.

[18:35] (planning next steps)
[18:35] Jordan: recap: i'll send the runbook + security pack + approximate pricing; priya will run initial capacity calc and share sizing spreadsheet; derek will send network details; lina will prepare eval prompts and an anonymized week of logs.
[18:50] Lina: agreed. I'll also share who in legal to contact for the DPA addendum.
[18:56] Marcus: is there a checklist we can use to track these items?
[19:02] Jordan: yes the onboarding runbook includes a checklist — we'll convert to a shared doc and invite you.

[35:00] (final Q&A and timeline check)
[35:00] Derek: one more question — for the batch embedding job, can Redwood run it inside our VPC to avoid egress?
[35:08] Priya: for Private/on-prem we can run entirely in your environment; for Dedicated with peering you can minimize egress. we'll clarify tradeoffs in the runbook.
[35:20] Marcus: ok pilot readiness target again? three weeks?
[35:25] Jordan: yes target pilot start ~2026-08-10 assuming all artifacts and peering are in place — that's three weeks plus some buffer.

[44:30] (wrap-up)
[44:30] Jordan: thanks everyone — final recap of next steps out loud:
[44:36] Jordan: 1) Jordan sends runbook + security pack by 2026-07-22.
[44:42] Jordan: 2) Priya shares capacity calc and sizing spreadsheet by 2026-07-24.
[44:47] Jordan: 3) Derek provides VPC/peering CIDRs and SAML metadata by 2026-07-23.
[44:53] Jordan: 4) Lina shares anonymized logs and 50 eval prompts by 2026-07-22.
[45:00] Marcus: ack, we'll aim for those dates.
[45:05] Jordan: i'll schedule a network walkthrough and tentative follow-up on 2026-07-27, i'll drop a calendar invite.
[45:12] Lina: thanks all.
[46:00] (meeting ends, small hold music)
